sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of default risk, accounting for roughly 28% of the model's importance, and risk rises steeply as the share of the credit limit in use goes up.
The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver, and risk increases with it, with the largest rise between no delinquencies and one or two.
The two features interact strongly: the effect of utilization is far larger for applicants with delinquencies, so high utilization combined with past delinquencies carries the greatest risk.
Annual income is among the next most important features, and risk decreases as income rises.
Length of credit history is also among the next most important features, and risk decreases as the history gets longer.
The debt-to-income ratio has a weak to moderate effect, and risk increases with it.
The data do not settle whether the number of dependents matters for default risk.
